item.title: any suggestions to make my SCP look better?: Re: any suggestions to make my SCP look better?
item.content:encoded:
Feedback
Read Below

A couple things here:

The entire page should be looked over for punctuation errors. Capitalization, commas, etc. It breaks immersion seeing a Foundation researcher write;

"by singing the song take on me by aha"

It should be:

"By singing the song Take On Me by Aha."

Revision 5159-A should be capitalized, and I highly recommend it is put in a quote box to separate it from the rest of the page.

- Audio from Skimmers radio during investigation

You should add who Skimmers is, before the log. I don't know if he is a government agent, an MTF officer, a scientist, etc. Example:

MTF Agent dispatched: Skimmers, John
Time: 0500 Dec 16, 2020
Reason for dispatch: Unknown anomalous presence

This gives more clarity on who he is. Remember, the Foundation documents basically everything. They are trying to study these things, and these documents are looked back upon for research in the future.

Interviewer: do you have a name?

SCP-5159: Yes, my name is Joseph Walker.

Here personally I don't think the Foundation really cares what his name is. They view him as an anomaly, not as a person. Staff are often very cold with the SCPs unless there is an anomalous or memetic reason not to be.

Also don't forget your rating module. A common mistake.

Other than that, good job.

item.title: any suggestions to make my SCP look better?: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
LongJumpingMan,

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: First SCP Draft: Re: First SCP Draft
item.content:encoded:
Hmmmm, the ways that the alter-Bens try to improve Ben ultimately are harmful to Ben's mental and at some points physical health. The other him do know this and therefore the worst-case scenario could involve Ben being completely disheartened by this and thinking that he can't improve at all and that these alternate versions of him are simply better than him/he doesn't feel like he can get to the points that all of them reached in their lives. Either way he gives up on trying to improve himself and falls back into a state of despair and spirals downwards thinking about his place in the world when so many other, better, versions of him exist.

Something like that could be the worst-case scenario, but I'm not quite sure how I would convey that idea in the story. Would he show doubt about his own abilities and keep comparing himself to them? Which they encourage more and more until he realises they aren't good for him? I don't know how I would go about that. But if any of that sounded like a good idea I could give it a shot.

item.title: Elevator draft, agaiin: Re: Elevator draft, agaiin
item.content:encoded:
It would be good to keep in mind I'm new to the foundation and haven't made an scp yet, so take my criticism with a grain of salt, but these are all the things I noticed while reading it, in the same order as the article.

my (nitpicky) criticism
 my (nitpicky) criticism

I don't get why it would be esoteric? seems like it would be safe, because they can just keep it in one place, no one else has access.

If the O-5 want people to give sightings of Dr. Spencer why would they cover his eyes? I would find a different image if you can't fully show that one.

The forewords are a bit confusing, I didn't immediately know you were talking about the d class, so some disambiguation about that would be good.

Another thing about Test 1 is Dr. Spencer seems oddly unclinical, his words themselves make grammatical sense but it definitely doesn't seem clinical. He should be stating things more factually, instead of words like "hey", "you're welcome", or "lots". It just seems like he should be less replying to the D class, and more telling him what to do in a stricter way.

The diary seems good to me, clinical tone isn't required obviously, but it does seem a bit hamfisted at the end there when he mentions the scp and how he wants to use it all in one sentence at the end.

I thought Test 2 was nice, but it felt a bit forced when you said "Always talked about the 1969 Moon landing". And again, I don't really think a doctor should be saying "hey" during procedure.

The second diary entry seemed better, because it was already established that he wanted to use the elevator, so I don't think a change needs to be present in my opinion.

I like that in the 3rd test, you specify that you're talking about the D-class this time, but I'm not sure why it didn't happen before. The Foreword of this is by far the best of the 3, it doesn't feel especially forced and gives a nice overview of the D class. The test itself seemed fine, but again, Dr. Spencer seems way too non-clinical. Also I don't think there's such a thing as Kauai Beach. Kauai is an Island in Hawaii, but I may be wrong on there being no beach.

Final diary is alright, but I'm confused how he managed to nab 2 pills of scp-500, as those are under super strict lockdown with weight sensors. I also thought the reference to 939 was forced, and there wasn't any mention of him working anywhere near those before.

Overall, the most glaring issues were it being esoteric, the test logs being non-clinical and there were a lot of things that came out of nowhere, like the 939 reference, the moon landing bit, or the sudden diary entry saying he wanted to use the elevator.

Although it might sound like I don't like it, I think this is actually a pretty solid idea, and one that could work really well. As was said in previous thread's criticism, there are other transportation scps, but I can't remember any very similar to this. I would also add a bit more to the description, like if they can interact with the other people there (if any), and if they can, what it looks like to the people in those locations when the elevator comes in (this could be determined by having someone go, finding out their favorite location, sending people to that area, then sending them again).
